text: 9.8 Vertical motion in air

label: Position and Movement
text: Under gravity only

label: Position and Movement
text: If an object is subject to the gravity only, it accelerates towards the Earth at a constant rate g which is roughly equal to 9.81 m s–2.

label: Position and Movement
text: Examples include an object released from a height and an object thrown vertically upwards.

label: Position and Movement
text: The acceleration due to gravity is always directed vertically downwards. If the upward direction is taken as positive, a minus (–) sign is assigned to g to indicate its direction.

label: Position and Movement
text: The acceleration due to gravity is independent of the mass, size and shape of an object if there is no air resistance acting on it.

label: Position and Movement
text: The process in which an object falls under gravity only is known as ‘free falling’.

label: Position and Movement

label: Position and Movement
text: The area under the v–t graph is the displacement of the stone.

label: Position and Movement
text: The slope of the v–t graph is –9.81. Therefore, the acceleration is –9.81 m s–2.

label: Position and Movement

label: Position and Movement

label: Position and Movement
text: The motion is symmetric. This can be illustrated by the symmetries about the dotted line in the s–t graph and the v–t graph.

label: Position and Movement

label: Position and Movement

label: Position and Movement

label: Position and Movement
text: Under gravity and air resistance

label: Position and Movement
text: The force exerted by the air to oppose the motion of a moving object is called the air resistance.

label: Position and Movement
text: The magnitude of the air resistance increases with the speed of the object.

label: Position and Movement
text: Consider an object which is released from rest. It accelerates at a rate of 9.81 m s–2 when it is just released. Take downward motion as positive.

label: Position and Movement
text: As the velocity of the object increases, the air resistance acting on it increases. The magnitude of the acceleration of the object will then decrease.

label: Position and Movement
text: When the weight of the object is balanced by the air resistance, the acceleration of the object becomes zero. The object now falls with a constant velocity which is called the terminal velocity.

text: 9.9 Devices used for recording motion

label: Position and Movement
text: Data-logging system

label: Position and Movement
text: A data-logging system consists of three main components: interface, computer software and various types of sensors.

label: Position and Movement
text: A motion sensor is used to study the motion of an object in a data-logging experiment.

label: Position and Movement
text: Time varying data collected by the sensor will be sent to the computer via the interface.

label: Position and Movement
text: The computer software can analyse and present the results in graph and table forms.

label: Position and Movement
text: The s–t graph, v–t graph and a–t graph can be generated and displayed on a computer screen.

label: Position and Movement
text: Advantages of using data-logging system:

label: Position and Movement
text: The data can be collected with high accuracy.

label: Position and Movement
text: It can measure changes over a very short period of time.

text: DSE 2015 (Paper 1B) Q4Exam Q4

label: Position and Movement
text: Stroboscopy

label: Position and Movement
text: Stroboscopy is a method used to capture instantaneous images of fast-moving objects.

label: Position and Movement
text: Stroboscope is able to emit intense flashlight at an adjustable frequency.

label: Position and Movement
text: The target object is illuminated by flashlight which lasts for about a millisecond (ms). The target object is apparently frozen to have its images recorded.

label: Position and Movement
text: All images of the target object are developed on the same photographic film so that they form a trajectory which is approximately same as that of the target object.

label: Position and Movement
text: The time interval between two successive images on the stroboscopic photo is 1f, where f is the flashing frequency. For an image taken at time t, its distance from the first image on the stroboscopic photo is equal to the displacement of the object at time t.

text: 10.1 Newton’s First Law of motion

label: Force and Motion
text: Newton’s First Law of motion states that:

label: Force and Motion
text: An object remains at rest or moves along a straight line with uniform speed if there is no net force or unbalanced force acting on it.

label: Force and Motion
text: Motion can occur in the absence of forces. Force is the cause of changes in motion.

label: Force and Motion
text: An unbalanced force (net force) acting on an object changes its speed and/or direction of motion.

label: Force and Motion
text: Inertia is the tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion.

label: Force and Motion
text: The inertia of an object is measured by its mass. An object with a large mass has larger inertia.

label: Force and Motion

label: Force and Motion
text: Force is a vector. It is measured in newtons (N).

label: Force and Motion
text: Friction

label: Force and Motion
text: • The direction of friction is opposite to the direction of velocity.

label: Force and Motion
text: • The magnitude of friction is independent of velocity.

label: Force and Motion
text: • The magnitude of friction between surfaces is independent of area in contact.

label: Force and Motion
text: Fluid resistance

label: Force and Motion
text: • The direction of fluid resistance is opposite to the direction of velocity.

label: Force and Motion
text: • The magnitude of fluid resistance increases with the speed of the object.

label: Force and Motion
text: • The magnitude of fluid resistance depends on the shape of the object. Fluid resistance acting on a streamlined shape object is smaller (F > F′).

label: Force and Motion
text: Weight

label: Force and Motion
text: • Weight is the force exerted on an object by the Earth.

label: Force and Motion
text: • Weight is always directed vertically downwards.

label: Force and Motion
text: Normal reaction

label: Force and Motion
text: • Normal reaction exists when two objects in contact press against each other.

label: Force and Motion
text: • Normal reaction is perpendicular to the contact surface.

label: Force and Motion
text: Tension

label: Force and Motion
text: • Tension is always directed along the string.

label: Force and Motion
text: • Tensions at the two ends of the string have the same magnitude and point into the string.

text: 10.4 Newton’s Third Law of motion

label: Force and Motion
text: Newton’s Third Law of motion states that:

label: Force and Motion
text: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

label: Force and Motion
text: When object A exerts a force (action) on object B, object B exerts on object A a force of equal magnitude in opposite direction (reaction).

label: Force and Motion
text: Examples of action-and-reaction pairs:

label: Force and Motion
text: F₁: gravitational force exerted by the Earth on the object

label: Force and Motion
text: F₂: gravitational force exerted by the object on the Earth

label: Force and Motion
text: R₁: normal force exerted by the object on the ground

label: Force and Motion
text: R₂: normal reaction exerted by the ground on the object

label: Force and Motion
text: T₁: tension exerted by block B on block A

label: Force and Motion
text: T₂: tension exerted by block A on block B

label: Force and Motion
text: F₁: downward force exerted by the rocket on the gas

label: Force and Motion
text: F₂: upward force exerted by the gas on the rocket

text: 10.5 Moment of a force

label: Force and Motion
text: The moment of a force τ about a point is a vector that measures its turning effect.

label: Force and Motion
text: Moment of a force about a point

label: Force and Motion
text: Couple

label: Force and Motion
text: A couple consists of two equal forces acting in opposite directions.

label: Force and Motion
text: The resultant force of a couple is zero but it produces a turning effect.

label: Force and Motion
text: Torque is the net moment of force produced by a couple.

label: Force and Motion
text: Torque = Perpendicular component of the force × Distance between the two forces

label: Force and Motion
text: Equilibrium of force

label: Force and Motion
text: An object is in equilibrium if it has no translational or rotational acceleration.

label: Force and Motion
text: A rigid object is in equilibrium if:

label: Force and Motion
text: no net or unbalanced force act on it, and

label: Force and Motion
text: total clockwise moment is equal to total anti-clockwise moment, i.e. the moment must be balanced.

label: Force and Motion
text: If the net moment about one point of an object is zero, then the net moment about any other points is zero as well.

label: Glossary
text: Glossary

label: Glossary
text: Key definitions from the notes in one place.

label: Glossary
text: Scalar

label: Glossary
text: A quantity with magnitude only, e.g. distance, speed, mass, density.

label: Glossary
text: Vector

label: Glossary
text: A quantity with both magnitude and direction, e.g. displacement, velocity, acceleration, force.

label: Glossary
text: Resultant

label: Glossary
text: The single vector produced when two or more vectors are added.

label: Glossary
text: Distance

label: Glossary
text: The length of the path taken by an object. It is a scalar.

label: Glossary
text: Displacement

label: Glossary
text: The shortest distance from the starting position to the final position. It is a vector and is independent of the path.

label: Glossary
text: Speed

label: Glossary
text: Distance travelled per unit time.

label: Glossary
text: Velocity

label: Glossary
text: Displacement per unit time; it tells how fast and in which direction an object moves.

label: Glossary
text: Uniform motion

label: Glossary
text: Motion with constant velocity: speed and direction both stay unchanged.

label: Glossary
text: Acceleration

label: Glossary
text: The rate of change of velocity, a = (v − u) ÷ t. Unit: m s⁻².

label: Glossary
text: Acceleration due to gravity (g)

label: Glossary
text: The constant acceleration of an object under gravity only, about 9.81 m s⁻² towards the Earth.

label: Glossary
text: Air resistance

label: Glossary
text: The force exerted by the air that opposes the motion of a moving object. It increases with speed.

label: Glossary
text: Terminal velocity

label: Glossary
text: The constant velocity reached when the weight of a falling object is balanced by air resistance.

label: Glossary
text: Data-logging system

label: Glossary
text: A system of sensors, an interface and computer software that records time-varying data and shows it as graphs and tables.

label: Glossary
text: Stroboscopy

label: Glossary
text: A method of capturing images of fast-moving objects using intense flashes at an adjustable frequency.

label: Glossary
text: Force

label: Glossary
text: A vector measured in newtons (N). An unbalanced force changes an object's speed and/or direction.

label: Glossary
text: Net force

label: Glossary
text: The resultant of all forces acting on an object; also called the unbalanced force.

label: Glossary
text: Inertia

label: Glossary
text: The tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion. It is measured by mass.

label: Glossary
text: Friction

label: Glossary
text: A force opposite to the direction of motion, independent of speed and of the area in contact.

label: Glossary
text: Weight

label: Glossary
text: The force exerted on an object by the Earth, always directed vertically downward.

label: Glossary
text: Normal reaction

label: Glossary
text: The force perpendicular to the contact surface when two objects press against each other.

label: Glossary
text: Free-body diagram

label: Glossary
text: A diagram showing all the forces acting on one object, drawn as arrows.

label: Glossary
text: Moment of a force

label: Glossary
text: The turning effect of a force about a point: perpendicular component of the force × distance from the point (N m).

label: Glossary
text: Couple

label: Glossary
text: Two equal forces acting in opposite directions. The resultant force is zero but there is a turning effect.

label: Glossary
text: Torque

label: Glossary
text: The net moment of force produced by a couple.

label: Glossary
text: Equilibrium

label: Glossary
text: A state with no translational or rotational acceleration: zero net force and balanced clockwise and anticlockwise moments.

label: Glossary
text: Centre of gravity

label: Glossary
text: The point where all the weight of an object can be considered to be concentrated.
